Author: @WineScrounger
Content: A common misconception about NDAs is that they can prevent you from reporting crimes. This isn’t true, never has been - NDAs are enforced under civil law, and criminal law trumps civil law wherever there is a conflict. So if your employer, customer or supplier (or anyone, really) has you sign an NDA and you later find out that they’re up to shady stuff, and you don’t want to get wrapped up in it, you absolutely can report them. I’m not a lawyer so talk to one first, but this is the case in US/UK law, and most parts of the world where law still has meaning.

Author: @DiarrheOfAMadBlackWoman
Content:
On a serious note: I went through something not _nearly_ as vile, but pretty bad for 5 whole years. Dude was my boss, well-respected, well-known, and established old white dude. He would withhold paychecks, threaten to cut off my health insurance (and I was very ill) and since he was the sole owner of his company, I had no one to talk to about it. It has taken me 3 yrs to finally take action and most days I literally can't bring myself to speak to anyone about it because I have a life. If I decide to go through old messages or e-mails, it's going to ruin my day, so it takes a TREMENDOUS amount of strength to come forward. It's scary, especially when the pervertedness also came with physical violence that he managed to wriggle out of in the courts... 

I know I need to do more as far as complying with certain organizations to bring him down, but I seriously can't put myself back in that place mentally. I wish I had someone else who could do it for me! So Cassie not only had to come forward, she had her entire personal life thrown to the public, she's had people talking about her just being a gold-digger, all sorts of nonsense. What money she has received, she DESERVES way, way more. That trauma doesn't go away. I still scream if someone comes into the same room as me and I didn't hear them first. I still have nightmares about that situation at least 6× a month AND I've been in therapy. Cassie? Good god, what she went through was SO much worse. 

I haven't seen a dime, nor do I expect to. However, if someone wants compensation, it's not just to live a life of leisure. Not only is it to guarantee you are OK financially even if you're unable to work due to all the trauma. Also, what's the best way to punish a greedy piece of garbage? Take their MONEY. It's their power, and by god I would want to take away some of that power, too. 

I'm rambling, but hearing how many times this happens, celebrities or just rich old dudes, is horrifying to me. The general public needs to put themselves into the shoes of the victims or, at the very least, pretend it's their mother, sister, aunt, whatever! Because what they're saying about Cassie? It says a lot about how women are perceived in this world.
